resolution: The tripwire's second strike confirmed real corruption (parsed doc.blob: v2, rangeCount 0 again) and its determinism cracked the case together with req_3058's zero-[rangetrace] observation: the flow reproduces because the HOST PROCESS OUTLIVES the user's window restarts — ModelView's resume path adopts the live host session and mirrors its ranges, so a session that lost its ranges once resumes degraded forever and every save persists the damage; no load path ever pushes (which is exactly why the tracer printed nothing). Restored Door_Wall_1 from git (second and third time) and fixed the resume path (c4acb58b6): resume now re-seeds the doc's saved ranges whenever the resumed host answers with fewer parts than the doc declares, logging the heal. The original one-time clearer is likely historical within the long-lived process; the req_3049 host-side tripwires will name any future clear after the pending rebuild.
